title: Ionic Bond and Its Properties
notes: **Ionic bond:** electrostatic attraction between oppositely charged ions formed by complete transfer of electrons from a metal to a non-metal.
**Formation example:** Na loses one electron to become Na$^+$, Cl gains one to become Cl$^-$. The oppositely charged ions attract to form NaCl.
**Lattice energy:** the energy released when gaseous ions combine to form one mole of solid ionic crystal. Higher lattice energy means a more stable ionic compound.

**Properties:** high melting and boiling points (strong electrostatic forces), brittle (like-charged ions repel when layers shift), conduct electricity when molten or dissolved (ions are free to move).
**Solubility:** most ionic compounds dissolve in polar solvents like water because water molecules stabilize the separated ions.
